login.title: Sign in
login.subtitle: Log in with your Twitch account to manage the bot for your channel.

scopes.title: What Twitch shares
scopes.email: The email address on file with Twitch.
scopes.moderatedChannels: The channels you moderate — this determines which channels you may manage here.
scopes.subscriptions: Your subscriptions — so sub-restricted votes know whether you may take part.
scopes.note: All three are read permissions. EmotePurge cannot write, post, or change anything on your behalf.

hero.title: Bring order to your 7TV emote set
hero.subtitle: EmotePurge shows you which emotes your chat actually uses, and removes the rest from 7TV in bulk — no guesswork.
hero.reading: After a few months, every active 7TV channel has accumulated hundreds of emotes — many long forgotten, never used, or not even wanted by the community. Figuring out by hand what's actually needed is tedious and subjective. EmotePurge turns that into a decision based on real chat data.

shape.caption: Schematic, with made-up numbers. The split into these four groups is the same one you'll see in your own set later.

measure.label: continuous
measure.title: Measure chat usage
measure.body: An anonymous bot sits in your channel's chat and keeps counting which emote is used how often. This is not a snapshot: because the raw data covers weeks, you pick the time range freely — the last seven days, the last month, everything since the join.

vote.label: optional
vote.title: Let the community vote
vote.body: For contested emotes you can let viewers, subs, or mods vote. You never have to — measured usage alone is enough.

purge.label: irreversible
purge.title: Remove from 7TV in bulk
purge.body: Flagged emotes leave your set in one go. That happens directly at 7TV and cannot be undone from here — which is why you select first, then confirm, then execute.

how.title: From login to a cleaned-up set

login.title: Log in with Twitch
login.body: One click is all it takes — no new password, no separate sign-up. Broadcasters, moderators, and 7TV editors automatically get exactly the permissions they are entitled to.

join.title: Join a channel
join.body: The bot joins your chat and syncs your active 7TV set.
join.note: Counting starts at the join. The first days are empty for that reason — not a bug, but the beginning of the measurement.

measure.title: Let it run
measure.body: Usage is recorded automatically while you do nothing. You can start a vote alongside it at any time.

purge.title: Clean up
purge.body: Pick emotes based on measured usage and remove them from 7TV in bulk.
purge.note: Deleting needs a 7TV token that you copy out of your browser's devtools once. 7TV offers no login for this. The token stays in your browser.

close.title: Ready to clean up your emote set?
close.subtitle: Log in with your Twitch account and get started right away.

twitch.body: EmotePurge asks Twitch for read permissions only: your email address, the channels you moderate, and your subscriptions. Nothing is ever written on your behalf.

token.body: The token that performs the deletion stays in your browser and is never sent to our server.

source.body: EmotePurge is open source under the GNU AGPL v3.

sevenTvToken.intro: To delete emotes you need your own 7TV write token from your logged-in 7tv.app session:
sevenTvToken.step1: Log in on 7tv.app (if you haven't already).
sevenTvToken.step2: Open dev tools (F12) → the "Application" tab (Chrome) or "Storage" tab (Firefox) → "Local Storage" → "https://7tv.app".
sevenTvToken.step3Prefix: Find the entry with the key
sevenTvToken.securityWarning: ⚠ This token grants full write access to your 7TV account (including deleting emotes). Treat it like a password — never share it. It stays only in this browser tab (sessionStorage), is never sent to our server, and is gone once you close the tab.
